title: Pull-back commutes with protocol execution
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with Alice's inputs drawn from $X$ and Bob's from $Y$, producing values in $\alpha$, and let $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ be arbitrary maps of input types. Then for all $x' \in X'$ and $y' \in Y'$, running the pull-back of $p$ along $f_X$ and $f_Y$ on the inputs $x'$ and $y'$ yields the same output as running $p$ itself on the transported inputs $f_X(x')$ and $f_Y(y')$.
hypotheses_covered: p is a protocol over X, Y with outputs in α
replaced:
For any protocol $p$ over $X \times Y$, input maps $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$,
and inputs $x' : X'$, $y' : Y'$,
\[
  (p.\texttt{comap}\;f_X\;f_Y).\texttt{run}\;x'\;y' \;=\; p.\texttt{run}\;(f_X\,x')\;(f_Y\,y').
\]
